## Purpose

Practice specifying CFA models in lavaan, and interpreting the results.

[**NOTE:** This is all fake data, specifically generated to highlight specific aspects of the lavaan model]{style="color:red;"}

Each scenario below gives you a research question, a description of the data,
and the sample covariance matrix. 

In this rlab, for each scenario:

1. Write the CFA model in lavaan syntax.
2. Fit the model and examine the global fit.
3. Interpret the results: the global fit, the standardized loadings, residual variances, and the factor correlation (if there is more than one factor).
4. Compare your results to the solutions.
5. Iterate until you get the same answers (or can make an argument for why yours are justified)

## Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
#| code-fold: false
library(tidyverse)
library(lavaan)
library(semPlot)
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
```{r}
#| include: false
# Teacher-only helpers. They live in a teacher block so they are stripped
# from the student .qmd download.
global_fit <- function(fit) {
  round(fitMeasures(fit, c("chisq", "df", "pvalue", "cfi", "tli",
                           "rmsea", "srmr")), 3)
}
path_diagram <- function(fit) {
  semPaths(fit, what = "path", whatLabels = "std", style = "lisrel",
           layout = "tree", rotation = 1, residuals = TRUE,
           intercepts = FALSE, nCharNodes = 0, sizeMan = 8, sizeMan2 = 4,
           sizeLat = 9, edge.label.cex = 1, edge.color = "black",
           color = list(lat = "lightblue", man = "white"),
           mar = c(4, 4, 4, 4))
}
```
:::

## Default model

Every scenario below uses the same `lavaan()` call. The arguments are already
set up in the templates:

- `sample_cov`, `sample_nobs` -- the data are a covariance matrix and a sample size.
- `auto_var = TRUE` -- freely estimate the variances (factor variances & residual variances).
- `auto_fix_first = TRUE` -- the first loading of each factor is fixed to 1 to set the scale.
- `auto_cov_lv_x = TRUE` -- factors are allowed to covary.
- `bad_marker_crit = 0` -- keep lavaan from swapping out the first indicator as the marker.

What you need to write is the model.

---

# Scenario 1

**Research question.** Do four subtests from a district mathematics assessment
reflect a single underlying **math proficiency**?

**The data.** A district gave **N = 350** 8th graders an assessment with four
subtests. Scores are on a 0--100 scale.

| Variable | Subtest                    |
|----------|----------------------------|
| `arith`  | Arithmetic computation     |
| `frac`   | Fractions & ratios         |
| `word`   | Word problems              |
| `estim`  | Estimation                 |

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
v1 <- c("arith", "frac", "word", "estim")
cov1 <- matrix(c(
   91.064,  62.996,  50.171,  40.210,
   62.996,  98.691,  51.044,  42.335,
   50.171,  51.044,  75.403,  32.401,
   40.210,  42.335,  32.401,  58.991),
  nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(v1, v1))

cov1
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# YOUR TURN
model1 <- "
  # ...your model here...
"
fit1 <- lavaan(model1,
                sample_cov = cov1, sample_nobs = 350,
                auto_var = TRUE, auto_fix_first = TRUE,
                auto_cov_lv_x = TRUE, bad_marker_crit = 0)

summary(fit1, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)
```

# Scenario 2

**Research question.** Are second-language (L2) learners' **motivation** to
learn English and their **anxiety** about using it two distinct, related
constructs?

answered six Likert items (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree).

| `q1`     | "I worry about making mistakes when I speak English" |
| `q2`     | "I enjoy learning English" |
| `q3`     | "I feel tense when I use English with native speakers" |
| `q4`     | "I put a lot of effort into my English classes" |
| `q5`     | "I get nervous when I have to speak English in class" |

```{r}
   -0.248,   0.756,  -0.419,   0.637,  -0.303,   0.999),
  nrow = 6, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(v2, v2))
```

# Scenario 3

**Research question.** Are **transformational leadership** and **team
psychological safety** two distinct, related constructs in work teams?

**The data.** A business-management researcher surveyed **N = 400** employees
about their manager and their team. All items are 1--5 agreement ratings, and
the matrix below is based on the responses as recorded. The researchers
developed the items for **leadership** (four items) and **safety** (four items).

| Variable | Item                                                        | Construct  |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| `x1`     | "It is safe to take a risk on this team" | Safety |
| `x2`     | "My manager coaches me to develop my strengths" | Leadership |
| `x3`     | "I usually eat lunch at my desk" | Safety |
| `x4`     | "My manager communicates a clear vision for the team" | Leadership |
| `x5`     | "It is difficult to ask other members of this team for help" | Safety |
| `x6`     | "My manager is on-site most days" | Leadership |
| `x7`     | "Team members can bring up problems and tough issues" | Safety |
| `x8`     | "My manager inspires me to do more than expected" | Leadership |

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
v3 <- c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7", "x8")
cov3 <- matrix(c(
  0.821,   0.270,   0.092,   0.316,  -0.581,   0.063,   0.535,   0.333,
  0.270,   0.895,   0.100,   0.543,  -0.320,   0.224,   0.337,   0.590,
  0.092,   0.100,   1.427,   0.160,  -0.162,   0.066,   0.077,   0.132,
  0.316,   0.543,   0.160,   0.943,  -0.392,   0.334,   0.401,   0.664,
 -0.581,  -0.320,  -0.162,  -0.392,   1.231,  -0.194,  -0.610,  -0.380,
  0.063,   0.224,   0.066,   0.334,  -0.194,   1.852,   0.185,   0.122,
  0.535,   0.337,   0.077,   0.401,  -0.610,   0.185,   1.029,   0.391,
  0.333,   0.590,   0.132,   0.664,  -0.380,   0.122,   0.391,   1.262),
  nrow = 8, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(v3, v3))

cov3
```

**Step 1.** Fit the model implied by the research question.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# YOUR TURN
model3 <- "
  # ...your model here...
"
fit3 <- lavaan(model3,
                sample_cov = cov3, sample_nobs = 400,
                auto_var = TRUE, auto_fix_first = TRUE,
                auto_cov_lv_x = TRUE, bad_marker_crit = 0)

summary(fit3, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)
```

**Step 2.** Examine AVE, shared variance, reliability, and residual correlations. 

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
std <- standardizedSolution(fit3)
load <- std[std$op == "=~", ]

# AVE for each factor
ave <- tapply(load$est.std^2, load$lhs, mean)

# Shared variance between factors (squared factor correlation)
fcor <- std$est.std[std$op == "~~" & std$lhs != std$rhs &
                      std$lhs %in% load$lhs]
shared <- fcor^2

# Reliability (omega) for each factor
resid <- std[std$op == "~~" & std$lhs == std$rhs & std$lhs %in% load$rhs, ]
theta <- resid$est.std[match(load$rhs, resid$lhs)]
sum_lam <- tapply(load$est.std, load$lhs, sum)
sum_theta <- tapply(theta, load$lhs, sum)
omega <- sum_lam^2 / (sum_lam^2 + sum_theta)

ave
shared
omega
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
resid_cor <- residuals(fit3, type = "cor")$cov
round(resid_cor, 2)
```

# Scenario 4

**Research question.** Are **depressive symptoms** and **anxiety symptoms**
distinct, related dimensions of distress among clinic patients?

**The data.** A clinical psychologist collected self-report data from
**N = 450** outpatients. Each item asks how often the symptom bothered the
patient over the last two weeks (0 = not at all, 3 = nearly every day). The
items were written to measure **depressive symptoms** (five items) and
**anxiety symptoms** (four items).

| Variable | Item                                       | Construct  |
|----------|--------------------------------------------|------------|
| `p1`  | Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge | Anxiety |
| `p2`  | Feeling down or sad | Depression |
| `p3`  | Difficulty finding parking at the clinic | Depression |
| `p4`  | Worrying too much about different things | Anxiety |
| `p5`  | Feeling hopeless about the future | Depression |
| `p6`  | Trouble relaxing | Anxiety |
| `p7`  | Little interest or pleasure in activities | Depression |
| `p8`  | Feeling worthless or like a failure | Depression |
| `p9`  | Not being able to stop or control worrying | Anxiety |

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
v4 <- c("p1", "p2", "p3", "p4", "p5", "p6", "p7", "p8", "p9")
cov4 <- matrix(c(
  0.571,   0.223,   0.020,   0.324,   0.217,   0.311,   0.242,   0.178,   0.307,
  0.223,   0.640,   0.100,   0.191,   0.438,   0.170,   0.461,   0.335,   0.191,
  0.020,   0.100,   0.872,   0.023,   0.039,   0.043,   0.079,   0.083,   0.014,
  0.324,   0.191,   0.023,   0.739,   0.222,   0.305,   0.221,   0.199,   0.613,
  0.217,   0.438,   0.039,   0.222,   0.722,   0.186,   0.418,   0.358,   0.199,
  0.311,   0.170,   0.043,   0.305,   0.186,   0.627,   0.175,   0.139,   0.317,
  0.242,   0.461,   0.079,   0.221,   0.418,   0.175,   0.839,   0.392,   0.193,
  0.178,   0.335,   0.083,   0.199,   0.358,   0.139,   0.392,   0.545,   0.165,
  0.307,   0.191,   0.014,   0.613,   0.199,   0.317,   0.193,   0.165,   0.673),
  nrow = 9, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(v4, v4))

cov4
```

**Step 1.** Fit the model implied by the research question.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# YOUR TURN
model4 <- "
  # ...your model here...
"
fit4 <- lavaan(model4,
                sample_cov = cov4, sample_nobs = 450,
                auto_var = TRUE, auto_fix_first = TRUE,
                auto_cov_lv_x = TRUE, bad_marker_crit = 0)

summary(fit4, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)
```

**Step 2.** Use modification indices to examine the model. Run this on your model from Step 1:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
modindices(fit4, sort. = TRUE, minimum.value = 10)
```

**Step 3.** Decide whether to free a parameter based on the modification indices. If you do, write the revised model, refit it, and compare to Step 1.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# YOUR TURN
model4b <- "
  # ...your revised model here...
"
fit4b <- lavaan(model4b,
                sample_cov = cov4, sample_nobs = 450,
                auto_var = TRUE, auto_fix_first = TRUE,
                auto_cov_lv_x = TRUE, bad_marker_crit = 0)

summary(fit4b, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)
```

**Step 4.** Examine AVE, shared variance, reliability, and residual correlations for your final model. (If you did not change the model, use `fit4` instead of `fit4b`.)

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
std <- standardizedSolution(fit4b)
load <- std[std$op == "=~", ]

# AVE for each factor
ave <- tapply(load$est.std^2, load$lhs, mean)

# Shared variance between factors (squared factor correlation)
fcor <- std$est.std[std$op == "~~" & std$lhs != std$rhs &
                      std$lhs %in% load$lhs]
shared <- fcor^2

# Reliability (omega) for each factor
resid <- std[std$op == "~~" & std$lhs == std$rhs & std$lhs %in% load$rhs, ]
theta <- resid$est.std[match(load$rhs, resid$lhs)]
sum_lam <- tapply(load$est.std, load$lhs, sum)
sum_theta <- tapply(theta, load$lhs, sum)
omega <- sum_lam^2 / (sum_lam^2 + sum_theta)

ave
shared
omega
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
resid_cor <- residuals(fit4b, type = "cor")$cov
round(resid_cor, 2)
```

```{r}
  dep =~ p2 + p7 + p5 + p8 + p3
  anx =~ p1 + p9 + p4 + p6
  p9 ~~ p4
"
fit4b <- lavaan(model4b,
                sample_cov = cov4, sample_nobs = 450,
                auto_var = TRUE, auto_fix_first = TRUE,
                auto_cov_lv_x = TRUE, bad_marker_crit = 0)
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer (Step 3, revised): AVE, shared variance & reliability (teacher)"}
```{r}
#| code-fold: false
std <- standardizedSolution(fit4b)
load <- std[std$op == "=~", ]

# AVE for each factor
ave <- tapply(load$est.std^2, load$lhs, mean)

# Shared variance between factors (squared factor correlation)
fcor <- std$est.std[std$op == "~~" & std$lhs != std$rhs &
                      std$lhs %in% load$lhs]
shared <- fcor^2

# Reliability (omega) for each factor
resid <- std[std$op == "~~" & std$lhs == std$rhs & std$lhs %in% load$rhs, ]
theta <- resid$est.std[match(load$rhs, resid$lhs)]
sum_lam <- tapply(load$est.std, load$lhs, sum)
sum_theta <- tapply(theta, load$lhs, sum)
omega <- sum_lam^2 / (sum_lam^2 + sum_theta)

ave
shared
omega
```
:::
